name: Order and Status Inquiries
h1: Order and Delivery Status Calls Answered From Your Own System
metaDescription: Callers ask where their order is. A Calldesk agent takes the order number, looks it up through your endpoint, and reads back the status or opens a request.
intro: Where is my order? is the call that never goes away. It arrives after every dispatch, every delay and every holiday, and the answer already exists in a system your staff must open to read aloud. The conversation is predictable: identify the order, find its status, explain what the status means and, when something has gone wrong, start a claim or a support request. That makes it a good fit for a voice agent, with one important condition. The agent must read real data, not guess. A knowledge base holds general answers, but an order status changes by the hour, so the lookup has to happen through a function step that posts the collected order number to an endpoint you control and uses the reply in the conversation. If you use HubSpot, there is also a lookup that returns a caller's contact fields as call-time variables. The order-status-checker and delivery-status-caller templates provide a flow in which the agent collects an identifier, confirms it by reading it back, retrieves status, explains next steps and opens a request for missing or damaged items. Staff then handle exceptions, not every routine check.
steps: Expose a read-access status endpoint on your side that accepts an order or tracking number and returns status text. Agree what it will say for unknown numbers.
Create an agent from the order-status-checker template and set the function step's webhook address to your endpoint.
Adjust the extraction step to collect the identifier you use and, if you need it, a second detail such as the name on the order or postcode.
Keep the read-back confirmation step, since misheard digits are the most common source of wrong answers.
Write a clear branch for exceptions, such as a package marked delivered but not received, that takes details and opens a support request through a second function step or a message.
Add a transfer for callers who ask for a person, publish, and test with real order numbers including wrong ones and ones in odd states.
Use the call-issues review and transcripts to check that number read-backs match what was said.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks for calling Oakridge Supply. I'm an AI assistant and I can check on an order for you. What's your order number?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: It's A as in apple, seven seven four two one.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Let me read that back: A, seven, seven, four, two, one. Is that right?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: One moment while I look that up.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Order A77421 shipped on Monday and is listed as out for delivery today.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Good. Last time it said delivered and nothing showed up.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I'm sorry about that. If it's marked delivered tonight and you don't have it, call back and I can start a missing package request. Anything else?

featuresUsed.howItHelps: The agent posts the collected order number to your endpoint and uses the reply as live status.
Order number, tracking number or name on the order are collected as fields and confirmed by read-back.
Where HubSpot holds your customers, a lookup by phone can supply their name and company as call-time variables.
Calls are analysed afterward for problems such as a number read-back mismatch, with the evidence listed.
Exceptions and upset callers can be passed to a person.
Staff see what was asked and what the agent said the status was.

considerations: Do not let the agent read personal or order details to an unverified caller. Decide what you require, such as a postcode or the name on the order, before status is shared.
Never take card numbers in this flow. Do not collect payment details unless you have designed and reviewed a payment process with counsel, which is outside this use case.
The agent is as current as your endpoint. If the system is down, script a graceful fallback that takes a message.

faq.q: Does Calldesk connect to my shop platform?
faq.a: There is no built-in connector for shop platforms. A function step posts to an endpoint you provide, so you or a developer need to supply one that returns the status.

faq.q: Can a knowledge base hold order statuses?
faq.a: A knowledge base suits stable facts. Order status changes continually, so use a function step to fetch it at call time.

faq.q: How does it handle misheard numbers?
faq.a: The template reads the identifier back for confirmation, and post-call checks flag number read-back mismatches in transcripts for review.

faq.q: Can it start a return or a claim?
faq.a: It can collect the details and post them to your endpoint, or leave them in the summary for staff. What happens next depends on your own process.

faq.q: What about callers who are not customers?
faq.a: Write a branch for an unknown order number that offers a message or transfer, and test it, since the failure path matters as much as the success path.
